WITH dept_counts AS (
  SELECT m.department AS department, COUNT(mem.member_id) AS member_count
  FROM member mem
  JOIN major m ON mem.link_to_major = m.major_id
  GROUP BY m.department
),
totals AS (
  SELECT SUM(member_count) AS total FROM dept_counts
),
shares AS (
  SELECT d.department, d.member_count, CAST(d.member_count AS REAL) / t.total AS share
  FROM dept_counts d
  CROSS JOIN totals t
),
avg_share AS (
  SELECT AVG(share) AS avg_share FROM shares
)
SELECT s.department, s.member_count, s.share, s.share - a.avg_share AS share_minus_avg
FROM shares s
CROSS JOIN avg_share a
WHERE s.share >= a.avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: Only members with a non-NULL link_to_major that matches a major_id are counted (inner join), so members without a valid major are excluded from the totals and shares.
The average share is the unweighted mean of the per-department shares, one value per department, as the request states.
A department with a NULL department value forms its own group rather than being dropped.
The >= comparison uses floating-point REAL values, so a department whose share equals the average only in exact arithmetic could fall on either side due to rounding error.
